resources.string:
Choose WhatsApp's sticker folder so the app can read your stickers. Access is read-only, and nothing leaves your phone: this app has no internet permission.

The folder is at:
Android › media › com.whatsapp › WhatsApp › Media › WhatsApp Stickers
No stickers match. Try other words, or long-press a sticker to add tags.
No stickers found yet. Check that you chose the WhatsApp Stickers folder.
This phone doesn\'t have enough memory to run the model. Search by printed text and tags still works.
Not enough free space. Importing needs about %1$s.
Couldn\'t import the file. Try again.
Before using %1$s, compare this SHA-256 with the one shown for the file on its download page. Only continue if they match.
Setting up the built-in model… This needs about 700 MB of free space; if it doesn\'t finish, free up some space and reopen the app.
Picture tags and search by meaning are built in and set themselves up. Both run only on this phone.

A small multilingual model finds stickers that mean what you typed, even with different words or in the other language: \"running late\" finds a sticker tagged \"מאחר\". It works best once stickers have picture tags. Stickers get ready for it while the phone charges.
Check how well search finds your stickers, and tune it, with test searches you write yourself.

Write searches the way you\'d really type them, in Hebrew and in English, and mark the stickers each one should find. Then run the test to see how often those stickers come up near the top. Everything stays on this phone.
%1$d test searches: %2$d Hebrew, %3$d English, %4$d mixed. Aim for about 50 Hebrew and 50 English.
That file isn\'t a test search export.
Search now uses the new cut-off.
Below target: the right sticker should be in the top 5 at least 80% of the time, with Hebrew within 5 points of English.
Each pair: share of right stickers in the top 5 / how high the first right one is (1.00 = first place).
Search by meaning isn\'t set up, so only keyword search was tested.
Search time: typically %1$d ms, slowest %2$d ms.
Similarity cut-off: now %1$s, best in this test %2$s.
%1$d test searches skipped: their stickers are no longer on this phone.
Searches that missed a right sticker in the top 5:
Test search, as you\'d type it
Tap every sticker this search should find. Use the box below to find them.
This text box doesn\'t accept stickers.
Stickers shared from this app arrive in WhatsApp as photos. To send real stickers, use the Peel-It keyboard: WhatsApp accepts stickers from keyboards, the same way Gboard sends them.
Android will warn that a keyboard can collect what you type. This one reads only your sticker search, only when you open it, and the app has no internet access.

1. In a WhatsApp chat, switch to the Peel-It keyboard (the keyboard button at the bottom of the screen, or long-press the space bar or globe key).
2. Type a few letters on its keys, in Hebrew or English (עב/EN switches). Results update as you type.
3. Tap a sticker. It's sent as a real sticker and your usual keyboard comes back.

If you already typed something in the chat box, the sticker keyboard searches for that, and removes it when you send.
What you type on its keys stays inside the keyboard. It reads at most 100 characters already in the chat box, only when you open it, never in password fields, and never saves them.

Builds a report to send to whoever helps you with the app: versions, index counts, background job states, recent crashes and the app\'s warning messages. It contains no stickers, file names, text from stickers, tags or searches. You\'ll see all of it before sharing.
That isn\'t the right file for this. Choose the %1$s file from the download page.
Turned off: the app crashed while this model was running, so it won\'t load again until you turn it on. If it crashes again, remove it and import the file again, checking it\'s the one named above.

A small image model (SigLIP 2), built into the app, looks at each sticker and tags what it shows — a cat, a laughing face, a birthday cake, Kermit — in Hebrew and English, so you can search for things that aren\'t written on the sticker. Nothing to install, and nothing leaves the phone.
Running now. Continues if you leave the app.
Runs by itself while the phone is charging, or start it now.
Find stickers of you, your friends and anyone else by name, including edits and inside jokes.
The app finds faces on your stickers and groups the same person\'s faces together. Name each group once, and every sticker with that face becomes searchable by the name, in Hebrew or English.
Each face is turned into a face fingerprint (biometric data). Fingerprints never leave this phone, aren\'t backed up, and you can delete them all at any time.
This build doesn\'t include the face models yet.
Looking for faces: %1$d of %2$d stickers left.
All stickers were checked for faces.
No groups yet. They appear as faces are found.
Tap a face that isn\'t this person to take it out of the group.
Take this face out of the group?
Turn off and delete face data
Delete all face fingerprints and group names? Your stickers stay; they just won\'t be searchable by these names anymore.
The joke, who it\'s about, when you send it…
Tap a wrong tag to hide it from search. Tap again to bring it back.

Only this edit is applied to the stickers you pick: tags you added are added and tags you removed are removed, picture tags you hid or brought back change the same way, and a changed description is copied. Nothing else on them changes. People names already apply to every sticker of that person.
None found. Picture tags or search by meaning may not have reached this sticker yet.

Something crashed, got stuck or found the wrong stickers? Build a report and send it with a line about what happened. It has counts, versions and error messages only: no stickers, file names, sticker text, tags, names or searches. You\'ll see all of it before sharing.

• Peel-It has no internet access: Android doesn't let it connect to anything, so nothing you do in it can leave the phone.
• It reads only the stickers folder you picked. The index, tags, people and settings are stored only in the app, and are left out of backups and phone-to-phone transfers.
• People is off until you turn it on. It turns faces into face fingerprints, which count as biometric data. Only use it on stickers of people who are OK with it, and you can delete all face data from the People screen at any time.
• The keyboard reads at most 100 characters already in the chat box, only when you open it, never in password fields, and never saves them.
• Uninstalling the app deletes everything it stored.
All run on this phone. They\'re downloaded when the app is built and checked against pinned fingerprints (SHA-256).
Peel-It is built with %1$d open-source libraries, most under the Apache License 2.0.
Updates only install over this app when they\'re signed with the same certificate. Its SHA-256 should match the one on the release page:
Peel-It\'s mascot, an elephant peeling a sticker
Suggested because this sticker looks like stickers you tagged. They\'re already searchable. Tap + to make one your tag, or ✕ to hide it.
